items.title: Lipschitz growth bounds every supplied subgradient · Optlib prerequisite

source.attribution: Hongjia Chen, Chenyi Li, Wanyi He, Zaiwen Wen, Optlib (Apache-2.0). Samplinglib native port and original exposition; not quoted textbook prose.

items.statement: For any globally G-Lipschitz real-valued function on a real inner-product space, every global supporting vector v at x satisfies ‖v‖≤G.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space with its associated norm. No completeness or finite-dimensionality assumption is imposed.
G is a nonnegative real Lipschitz constant and f:E→ℝ is globally G-Lipschitz.
SupportsAt f x v means f(x)+⟨v,z−x⟩≤f(z) for every z∈E. It supplies a genuine global supporting vector; no differentiability or totalized gradient is used.

obligations.label: For any globally G-Lipschitz real-valued function on a real inner-product space, every global supporting vector v at x satisfies ‖v‖≤G.

bindings.boundary: No existence or measurable selection of supporting vectors is claimed. The theorem does not require convexity once a global supporting vector is supplied, just as the corresponding upstream direction. This is a native local port of the norm bound, not a bulk import of Optlib or a sampling convergence result.

assumption_deltas.source: Global real Hilbert supporting-vector inequality and NNReal Lipschitz constant.
assumption_deltas.lean: Existing SupportsAt predicate is the same inequality; no differentiability, chosen global optimizer or norm-bound premise.
assumption_deltas.reason: Upstream SubderivAt membership is unbundled into its literal supporting inequality. No theorem conclusion is moved into the inputs.

items.title: The actual subgradient steps telescope weighted objective gaps · Optlib prerequisite

source.attribution: Hongjia Chen, Chenyi Li, Wanyi He, Zaiwen Wen, Optlib (Apache-2.0). Samplinglib native port and original exposition; not quoted textbook prose.

items.statement: Let f be globally G-Lipschitz. For sequences x_k,v_k and nonnegative real steps a_k, suppose v_k supports f at x_k and x_(k+1)=x_k−a_k v_k for every k. For every comparator z and every N≥0, the weighted objective gaps obey the displayed bound, including the terminal squared distance.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space with its associated norm. No completeness or finite-dimensionality assumption is imposed.
G is a nonnegative real Lipschitz constant and f:E→ℝ is globally G-Lipschitz.
SupportsAt f x v means f(x)+⟨v,z−x⟩≤f(z) for every z∈E. It supplies a genuine global supporting vector; no differentiability or totalized gradient is used.
x,v:ℕ→E and a:ℕ→ℝ. Each a_k≥0; each v_k supports f at x_k; the update x_(k+1)=x_k−a_k v_k is an exact equality.
z is any comparator in E, not a supplied minimizer. N is any natural number, including zero. There is no division by a step or horizon.

obligations.label: Let f be globally G-Lipschitz. For sequences x_k,v_k and nonnegative real steps a_k, suppose v_k supports f at x_k and x_(k+1)=x_k−a_k v_k for every k. For every comparator z and every N≥0, the weighted objective gaps obey the displayed bound, including the terminal squared distance.

bindings.boundary: This exposes the stronger weighted intermediate estimate used by the upstream convergence proof. It does not assert monotonicity of function values or a last-iterate rate. The source uses positive steps; allowing zero steps and N=0 here is an explicit division-free generalization, not a repair. No stochastic oracle, kernel or expected sampling cost is constructed.

assumption_deltas.source: Global real Hilbert supporting-vector inequality and NNReal Lipschitz constant.
assumption_deltas.lean: Existing SupportsAt predicate is the same inequality; no differentiability, chosen global optimizer or norm-bound premise.
assumption_deltas.reason: Upstream SubderivAt membership is unbundled into its literal supporting inequality. No theorem conclusion is moved into the inputs.

assumption_deltas.source: Source algorithm positive steps; proof intermediate with a terminal distance.
assumption_deltas.lean: Nonnegative steps and N=0 also permitted in a division-free weighted estimate.
assumption_deltas.reason: Zero steps/empty sum are algebraic endpoint extensions; not normalized at zero.

items.title: A finite run contains a subgradient iterate with the convergence bound · Optlib prerequisite

source.attribution: Hongjia Chen, Chenyi Li, Wanyi He, Zaiwen Wen, Optlib (Apache-2.0). Samplinglib native port and original exposition; not quoted textbook prose.

items.statement: Under the same Lipschitz, support and exact-update assumptions, suppose every step is strictly positive and N>0. For any comparator z, some index i<N satisfies the displayed normalized best-iterate objective-gap bound.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space with its associated norm. No completeness or finite-dimensionality assumption is imposed.
G is a nonnegative real Lipschitz constant and f:E→ℝ is globally G-Lipschitz.
SupportsAt f x v means f(x)+⟨v,z−x⟩≤f(z) for every z∈E. It supplies a genuine global supporting vector; no differentiability or totalized gradient is used.
x,v:ℕ→E; a:ℕ→ℝ with a_k>0; each v_k supports f at x_k; x_(k+1)=x_k−a_k v_k for every k.
N>0, so the finite index set is nonempty and the sum of its positive step sizes is strictly positive.
z is arbitrary. Neither attainment of the global infimum nor differentiability is supplied.

obligations.label: Under the same Lipschitz, support and exact-update assumptions, suppose every step is strictly positive and N>0. For any comparator z, some index i<N satisfies the displayed normalized best-iterate objective-gap bound.

bindings.boundary: The upstream theorem writes the best finite value as a real sInf over k+1 iterates. An actual minimizing index is equivalent on this nonempty finite set; N>0 corresponds to its k+1 horizon. No claim is made about the last iterate, existence of subgradient selectors, asymptotic iterate convergence, stochastic selection, PBPS/SPHMC or sampling complexity. These are reusable Optlib-source components placed beside Optimisation Chapter6; the complete Chewi chapter statement/route is not silently declared finished.
